questions.q: Priorat's climate is hot and dry Mediterranean. What does the Court's Certified cell add about it?
questions.exp: The Court's Certified climate cell for Priorat reads significant diurnal shifts. Summer days pass 35 °C, but the altitude of the hills, up to about 750 metres, and the ring of ranges around the bowl bring cool nights that keep acidity and freshness in Garnacha and Cariñena.

questions.q: Which way of training Priorat's old vines does the Court name, asking a candidate to recognise it in a photograph?
questions.exp: The Court's Certified grape growing cell names bush vine (gobelet) training: a free-standing vine with short arms spurred from the head of the trunk and no wire. On Priorat's slate it gives naturally low yields, and the same form is the alberello of southern Italy and the en vaso of Spain.

questions.q: What does Priorat's steep terrain rule out in the vineyard, by the Court's account?
questions.exp: The Court says Priorat's terrain does not allow for mechanisation. Old bush vines on narrow terraces and on the costers, slopes planted straight up the hillside, are pruned and picked by hand, and the slate holds so little water that each vine carries only a handful of bunches.

questions.q: Which machine does the Court say Cava producers typically use instead of riddling by hand?
questions.exp: The Court's Introductory winemaking cell says Cava typically uses the gyropalette, which it calls a Spanish invention, instead of riddling by hand. The machine turns a cage of several hundred bottles in programmed steps over a few days, where a pupitre, the hand riddling rack, takes weeks.

questions.q: Which white grape, Priorat's leading white, does the Court add for Catalonia at the Certified level?
questions.exp: Garnacha Blanca, Garnatxa Blanca in Catalan, is the Court's Certified white for Catalonia beside international varieties. On Priorat's slate it leads rich, stony dry whites with Macabeu and Pedro Ximénez, while Xarel-lo, Parellada and Macabeo remain the Introductory Cava grapes.

questions.q: Which international red grape does the Court name for Catalonia at the Certified level?
questions.exp: The Court's Certified red grapes for Catalonia are Pinot Noir and other international red varieties. Pinot Noir is permitted in Cava for white and rosado wines, while Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah came into Priorat's blends with the pioneers of the 1980s; Zinfandel, Nebbiolo and Pinotage play no part here.

questions.q: A Cava de Guarda needs at least nine months on its lees. What minimum does the Court give for a Cava Reserva?
questions.exp: The Court's Certified cell gives Cava (Cava de Guarda) a minimum of nine months on the lees and Reserva eighteen. Under the rules applied from 2022, Reserva, Gran Reserva at thirty months and Cava de Paraje Calificado at thirty-six form the vintage-dated Cava de Guarda Superior family; fifteen months is the minimum for Clàssic Penedès.

questions.q: Which oak does the Court say is common in Priorat's modern winemaking?
questions.exp: The Court's Introductory winemaking cell says modern winemaking, including the use of French oak, is common in Priorat. The Gratallops pioneers of the late 1980s aged their wines in new French barriques; many houses now prefer larger and older casks, but French oak remains the norm, unlike the American oak of traditional Rioja.

questions.q: Cava may be made across Spain. Within which DO of Catalonia does the Court say the vast majority is made?
questions.exp: The Court's Certified cell says DO Cava covers all of Spain, but the vast majority is made within the Penedès DO of Catalonia, above all around Sant Sadurní d'Anoia. DO Penedès is a separate geographic denomination for still wines and for Clàssic Penedès, its own traditional method sparkling.

questions.q: The Court asks for the significance of one Priorat village's project in the late 1980s. Name the village.
questions.exp: At Gratallops a small group of newcomers made their first vintage, 1989, in one shared cellar and sold it as five clos wines: destemmed fruit, long macerations and new French oak. The project gave Priorat its modern style and its reputation, which is why the Court calls Priorat a modern wine that made a big impact in a short time.

questions.q: Which of these clos wines stands on the Court's list of Priorat producers?
questions.exp: Clos Erasmus is one of the Court's Priorat producers, with Clos Mogador, Clos Martinet and Scala Dei, all names from the Gratallops revival or the old priory. Clos de Vougeot is a Burgundy grand cru, Clos Sainte Hune an Alsace Riesling and Clos du Mesnil a single-vineyard Champagne.

questions.q: A young Priorat is ripe, intense, oaky and high in alcohol. Which dish suits it best?
questions.exp: The Court asks how Priorat's oak, ripeness, intensity and alcohol affect a pairing. Its weight and firm tannin need a dish of equal richness, such as braised lamb, game or a stew; alcohol fans the heat of chilli, and the wine swamps delicate oysters or a light goat's cheese salad.
